visualReview.notes: Actually inspected all 13 current portable views and all 51 current frame contact views, including eight architectural cameras. Compared with seven individually viewed local originals (current 2025 west aerial; 2006 west; 2007 north; 2012 east/north; 2014 tower/approach; two 2009 terrace/bridge views), all 61 candidate contacts and the owner guide’s current plan. Actual five gallery arches, old-mill boat passage, separate arched entry bridge, north three-bay house, polygonal pointed-glazed chapel, projecting east study, four conical turrets, tall stone chimneys, roof valley and open clock lantern. Nine gallery windows and oculus dormers per long face; round-headed bays and upper lookouts align with four native bridge piers. Detached Marques Tower retains corbelled upper floor, attached stair turret, main cone, chimney and open cupola. Own terrace retaining walls, paving, well, entry balcony/corbels and six steps. Repairs corrected the gallery’s signed alignment, hidden glazing on curved applied faces, chapel edge orientation, a missing entrance landing and upper panels/windows misplaced relative to bridge piers.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Actually inspected all 13 final shared-material views, including north-up placement. Seven authored groups resolve to five shared limestone, plain concrete, weathered limestone, slate and painted-metal identities; opaque glazing and oak doors use local palette colors. Pale upper masonry, darker water-contact bases, charcoal slate roofs and original simplified geometric relief. No façade photographs, copied heraldry or generated bitmap textures. Synthetic library ground intentionally exposes/hides some below-datum supports; only the independent terrain preview and numerical controls certify the bounded site contact.

mediumFiReview.notes: Actually inspected all 25 current version-2 lighting/quality, silhouette, eight architectural-detail and four forced-distance frames. Canonical intended asset/runtime/selected level verifies in each. Explicit 954 / 3556 / 15993 / 58112 triangle levels satisfy their budgets. Skyline retains the five gallery arch voids, mill passage, separate approach bridge, main house/turrets/chimneys, both open lanterns, detached tower/stair turret and terrace. District restores three principal dormers per house face, nine gallery dormers per side, palette windows and selected balcony/rail counters. Street restores true gallery and chapel window recesses, cornices, leaded-window rhythm and bridge rails; main-house and curved tower glazing remains applied at this distance. Close adds main-house true window recesses, turned balusters, finer pointed tracery, original dormer details and small lead bars. Synthetic neighbors and beige water-surface terrain are context; no live hydrology or physical-device performance claim.

geographicReview.notes: Signed native own-house/gallery/chapel/tower outlines and immediate terrace island only. Separate gardens, Chancellerie/orangery, south service annex and all neighbors excluded. +X west/south-west across the gallery; +Z north/north-west toward the entrance terrace. 2025 actual local aerial and seven original exterior/approach views corroborate the composition. Owner 60×6m gallery dimensions are internal room controls and did not rescale the approximately 63m exterior gallery. Original Terrarium baseline (two original PNGs and original grid/height field) is preserved but rejected: its near-flat river/terrace values would bury the arches. Before geometry, independently acquired unchanged official IGN response values resolve the river about 6.52m below the dry terrace datum of 60.84m. All 25921 values and six exact requests/responses verify; no effective native resolution or surveyed accuracy is inferred from the 2m review grid. Provider water surface is source-epoch hydrology, not riverbed or live water. Supports extend to −12m. Own native terrace paving at +0.25m clears all 546 in-island original grid nodes by at least 0.03m; original terrain remains unchanged. Actual arch crowns clear provider river surface by over four metres. This is a bounded preview; hosts using the rejected coarse ground need compatible terrain before activation. Footprint replacement disabled.

fidelityReview.scope: Main river château, five-arch gallery, chapel, detached Marques Tower and immediate raised approach terrace.
fidelityReview.notes: Three exact2022Hermann Luyken CC0 exteriors confirm the pale main logis,corner conical towers,steep slate roof/dormers/chimneys,separate Tour des Marques,chapel projection and long two-storey gallery over five open river arches. Current mapped plan and model retain these identifying relationships. West gallery and five-arch current renders were inspected alongside the exact natives. Fine sculpture,individual stone joints,hidden roof valleys and precise water/threshold levels remain medium-fi estimates. Gardens,river scenery and interiors are outside scope. Accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi exterior scope. No reference pixels are embedded. Previously used attribution/private imagery is excluded from this current review.

runtimeLodReview.notes: Four authored Float32 meshes and four actual imported GLTFLoader meshes pass finite attributes, winding, normal and color validation. All 399 actual-runtime controls pass: five principal arch voids and pylon closures, unchanged river clearance, mill passage/supports, north approach arch, both open lanterns, balcony counters, close main-house and street/close gallery window recesses/glazing, and six visible entry treads. All LODs preserve the major openings. Independent grid controls additionally check 546 terrace nodes. Palette/distant silhouettes and applied main-house/tower windows at intermediate distances are deliberate simplifications; close true gallery/main-house recesses and physical bridge voids remain distinct.

geometryValidation.notes: Source/import and four detail levels, strict medium-fi audit, source/scene/terrain/placement schemas, actual asset inspection, matching repeated 30-tick states, six runtime-pack members and default preview query pass. All 51 current renders actually inspected; all 25 canonical medium-fi frame identities verify. All original provider values, request/response hashes, rejected baseline source hashes and PNG16 round trip verify. No independent Khronos or physical-device performance certification.

limitations: Seven local originals individually inspected and all 61 candidate contacts reviewed. Many other candidates are interiors, other Loire châteaux, historical illustrations or an unbuilt grand proposal; they do not control current exterior geometry.

Main house, river gallery/five principal arches, mill foundation/boat arch, chapel, detached Marques Tower, immediate raised terrace and short approach bridge only. Gardens, Chancellerie, orangery, separate south service annex, landscape, people, interiors, heraldic inscriptions and photo textures excluded.

Native generalized map part heights are massing hints, not surveys. Owner gallery dimensions are internal. Fine carving, unobserved details, roof engineering, thresholds and vertical levels are conservative photo-based estimates.

Terrain acquisition precedes geometry. Original source pixels and sampled relief must remain unchanged. River DEM is a composite water/terrain surface and supplies no reliable bathymetry or current water level; no surveyed riverbed compatibility is claimed.

Gallery five principal arches and separate mill/entry bridge openings must remain actual voids in all four LODs. Nine gallery windows and nine oculus dormers per long face derive from the photographs and the owner’s 18-window total.

RGE ALTI products are available at 1m and 5m grid spacing. This API resource does not expose the effective source resolution or surveyed accuracy at this site; neither is asserted. Building/bridge areas may be interpolated in the terrain product.
Hydrographic surface levels are source-epoch values, not bathymetry, live water levels or engineering clearance.
Default Terrarium baseline does not resolve the river/raised terrace and is explicitly rejected, preserved and hash-bound; terrain compatibility requires the independent higher-resolution field.
